audit.why: 45.40% over 696 games — the worst matchup in this slice alongside Urgot. Two free levels, then his sustain catches the poke and Infinite Duress ends the discussion.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven stages are sided Jayce in a 45% matchup. whys[2] says 'the window is closing fast', whys[3] says 'trades stop netting you value', whys[4] calls one R 'a death sentence', whys[5] says his first sustain item 'out-heals your combo burst', and late says 'This is where you lose'.
audit.why: The chart claims Jayce owns both item stages and levels 4-5 while every caption under them describes Warwick taking over. Packet reference chart Jayce|Jayce|Skill|Warwick|Warwick|Warwick|Warwick matches the text and the win rate.
audit.corrected: Sides re-set to Jayce, Jayce, Skill, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl (E) is not mentioned anywhere on the page. Riot: 'Warwick gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to FLEE for 1 second.' Also Jaws of the Beast is called a 'bite-heal' without saying it deals damage based on the target's MAXIMUM HEALTH.
audit.why: The fear is the ability that actually breaks a Jayce combo in lane — it walks you out of Lightning Field and out of Hammer range mid-rotation, and it is up every 15 seconds, far more often than his 110s ult. Leaving it out means the page blames the ult for losses the E caused. And max-health damage is an itemisation fact: health stacking feeds it, which is flagged for this matchup.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl's damage reduction and 1s fear stated in mid and whys[3]; the max-health bite stated in late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Flagged defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere.
audit.why: Jaws of the Beast 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s, Blood Hunt 80/70/60/50/40s, Primal Howl 15/14/13/12/11s, Infinite Duress 110/90/70s with a 1.5-second suppression. The 15s Primal Howl is the cooldown that decides lane trades; the 110s R is the one that decides the game.
audit.corrected: 15s Primal Howl and the 1.5s suppression stated in mid.

edits.before: Your Cannon-Q to swap-shred (the first hit after each R stance-swap cuts his Armor and MR) into Hammer To-the-Skies, E, W is a real burst at 2-3, but if he is already low his Q drain refunds most of it, so only commit the full combo when he is above half and his heal does less. From level 6 the lane inverts: Infinite Duress leaps in and locks an unstoppable multi-hit suppress, and you build zero defensive stats, so one R holds you for his entire combo. You cannot pull him off mid-channel, so the rule is positioning, never give him a flank or a gap to leap from, and hold your Thundering Blow E to knock him out of the leap before it lands or to peel the instant he commits.
edits.after: Your Cannon-Q to swap-shred (the first hit after each R stance-swap cuts his Armor and MR) into Hammer To-the-Skies, E, W is a real burst at 2-3, but if he is already low his Q drain refunds most of it, so only commit the full combo when he is above half. Watch Primal Howl: 2.5 seconds of damage reduction and then a FEAR on everyone nearby for 1 second, up every 15s — that is what walks you out of your own combo, not his ult. From level 6 the lane inverts: Infinite Duress leaps in and suppresses you for 1.5 seconds, and you build zero defensive stats. You cannot pull him off mid-channel, so the rule is positioning, never give him a flank or a gap to leap from, and hold your Thundering Blow E to knock him out of the leap before it lands.

edits.before: His passive sustain catches up to your poke and Blood Hunt punishes any HP you spend, so trades stop netting you value.
edits.after: Primal Howl's damage reduction and fear break your combo, his max-health Q bite heals him back, so trades stop netting you value.

edits.before: This is where you lose if the game gets here. Your damage falls off, your frame stays paper-thin, and his drain plus the heal-on-low-HP passive means he simply out-DPS-and-heals you in any extended fight, while Blood Hunt re-detects every low target to chain-chase your whole team. Anti-heal is non-negotiable, but it only slows the bleed. Spend every early edge before two items, play for picks and side-lane pressure with your stance-swap mobility, and never be the isolated target his R goes looking for.
edits.after: This is where you lose if the game gets here. Your damage falls off, your frame stays paper-thin, and Jaws of the Beast bites a share of your MAX health and heals him for it, so stacking HP feeds him while Blood Hunt re-detects every low target to chain-chase your team. Anti-heal is non-negotiable, but it only slows the bleed. Spend every early edge before two items, play for picks and side-lane pressure with your stance-swap mobility, and never be the isolated target his R goes looking for.

notes: Primal Howl was absent from the entire page — 2.5s of damage reduction then a 1-second fear on a 15s cooldown, which is the ability that actually breaks a Jayce combo in lane. Jaws of the Beast deals max-health damage, so health stacking is the wrong answer. I did NOT touch the claim in spikes[2] and mid that you cannot knock Warwick off Infinite Duress mid-channel: Riot's description is silent on it and the kit file's derived flags say the opposite ('channel: interruptible — any CC cancels it'), so it is unresolved and I would not overwrite either way without a ruling.
